newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Canada plans daily Paris-Toronto 747 co.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada plans daily Paris-Toronto 747 co.

text.p: Air Canada said it will have a daily Boeing 747-400 combi on its Paris-Toronto route from June 2.
Last year, during the same period, Air Canada operated Boeing 767-200 and 767-300 passenger aircraft on the route .

"The introduction of the combis on the route will significantly increase our ex-Europe lift compared to last year and our French cargo station will share capacity with Germany, Italy and Spain," Air Canada's cargo sales and services manager, France and Western Europe, Daniel Bregere said.

He added: "As far as France-originating freight is concerned, the combis will mean a little more capacity is available on last year, while there will also be scope to accomodate outsize shipments from our French customers which with the 767s we were hardly in a position to accept," he added.
Air Canada's Paris-Toronto combis, operating until end-October, will be backed up with four weekly 767-200 flights on the same route.

The Canadian carrier is also providing a daily Paris-Montreal service, using a 747 passenger aircraft and a three times weekly Paris-Vancouver service using 767-300s. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+171-542-7706 Fax +5017
